us-texas.title: Flag of Texas (Lone Star)
desc:
- The flag of Texas — the 'Lone Star Flag' — has a vertical blue stripe at the hoist bearing a white five-pointed star, alongside two horizontal stripes of white (top) and red (bottom)
- Adopted on 25 January 1839 during the Republic of Texas era, it is one of only two US state flags that previously served as the flag of an independent nation (the other is Hawaii)
- **Construction:** a blue vertical stripe occupying one-third of the fly at the hoist, with a white five-pointed star centred
- Two horizontal bands of white (top) and red (bottom) fill the remaining two-thirds
- Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- Texas's flag was the national flag of an independent republic (1836–1845) before statehood
- The Lone Star represents Texas's independence and pride
- Texas adopted this flag in 1845

us-hawaii.title: Flag of Hawaii

colors.note: The Hawaiian monarchy and naval tradition.
The Hawaiian monarchy and British influence.

desc: - The Hawaiian flag uniquely features the Union Jack in its canton — the only US state flag to include the flag of a foreign country, reflecting Hawaii's historical ties to Britain
trivia:
- Hawaii's flag uniquely features the Union Jack, reflecting its early relationship with Britain
- The eight stripes represent Hawaii's major islands
- Hawaii adopted this flag in 1845 during the Hawaiian Kingdom period

us-puerto-rico.title: Flag of Puerto Rico
desc:
- Five alternating red and white horizontal stripes with a blue isosceles triangle at the hoist bearing a white five-pointed star
- Adopted in 1895 by the Puerto Rican section of the Cuban Revolutionary Party, the flag was inspired by the Cuban flag with inverted colours
- It became the official flag of Puerto Rico in 1952
- **Construction:** five equal horizontal stripes alternating red and white (red at top and bottom)
- A blue equilateral triangle at the hoist with a white star
- Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- Puerto Rico uses the US flag but has its own distinct local flag
- The flag colours represent the five ethnic groups
- Puerto Rico is an unincorporated US territory with a strong local cultural identity

us-washington-dc.title: Flag of the District of Columbia
desc:
- Two horizontal red stripes below three red five-pointed stars on a white field — based on the coat of arms of George Washington's family
- Adopted on 15 October 1938, the design derives from the heraldic banner of the Washington family, which had used this pattern since at least the 14th century in England
- It has become an icon of DC statehood advocacy
- **Construction:** a white field with two horizontal red bars in the lower portion and three red five-pointed stars arranged horizontally above
- Ratio 10:17
trivia:
- Washington DC's flag features three red stars and two red bars
- Represents the District of Columbia
- DC is the nation's capital and seat of federal government

us-new-york.title: Flag of New York
desc: - The dark blue field bears the state coat of arms: two female figures (Liberty and Justice) flanking a shield with a Hudson River sunset scene
- **Construction:** a dark blue field bearing the state coat of arms centred — two female figures (Liberty and Justice) flanking a shield depicting a sun rising over the Hudson Highlands
trivia:
- The seal shows an eagle and shield representing American strength and New York's heraldry
- The shield contains symbols representing commerce, agriculture, and freedom
- New York adopted this flag in 1901

us-alaska.title: Flag of Alaska
desc: - Designed by 13-year-old Benny Benson in 1927, featuring the Big Dipper and Polaris (North Star) in gold on a dark blue field
- **Construction:** a dark blue field bearing eight gold five-pointed stars — seven forming the Big Dipper constellation and one (larger) representing Polaris, the North Star
trivia:
- Alaska's flag features the Big Dipper and Polaris (North Star), representing the state's northern location
- The constellation and star were chosen for their navigation significance to Alaska
- Alaska adopted this flag in 1927; the design emphasizes the state's unique geography

us-maryland.title: Flag of Maryland
desc: - One of the most distinctive US state flags, displaying the heraldic banners of the Calvert and Crossland families — Lord Baltimore's coat of arms
- **Construction:** quartered diagonally, alternating the Calvert family arms (gold and black paly with a diagonal band) and the Crossland arms (red and white cross bottony)
trivia:
- The heraldic quarters represent the Calverts (proprietors) and the Barons Baltimore
- Maryland's flag is unique among US states with its intricate heraldic design
- Maryland adopted this flag in 1904

us-new-mexico.title: Flag of New Mexico
desc:
- The Zia sun symbol in red on a golden-yellow field. The Zia is a sacred symbol of the Zia Pueblo people representing the circle of life
- **Construction:** a field of Spanish yellow bearing the Zia sun symbol in red, centred
- The Zia symbol has four groups of four rays extending from a central circle
trivia:
- The Zia Sun symbol comes from the Zia Pueblo Native American people
- The four rays represent the four cardinal directions and four sacred obligations
- New Mexico adopted this flag in 1925, making it one of the newest state flag designs

us-arizona.title: Flag of Arizona
desc: - The copper star represents Arizona's mining industry, with thirteen red and gold rays symbolising the original colonies and western sunsets
- **Construction:** the lower half is a blue field; the upper half has thirteen alternating red and yellow rays emanating from a central copper-coloured star
trivia:
- The copper star (blue) represents Arizona's copper mining heritage
- The rays represent the sunset; the colours represent the natural beauty of the desert
- Arizona adopted this flag in 1910

us-colorado.title: Flag of Colorado
desc:
- Three horizontal stripes of blue, white, and blue with a red 'C' encircling a golden disc on the left side
- Adopted on 5 June 1911 (with the current design fixed in 1964), the 'C' stands for Colorado, coloured red for the state's namesake (ruddy earth)
- The gold disc represents abundant sunshine
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands of blue (top), white, and blue
- The red 'C' is centred on the left third with a gold circle filling its opening
- Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- The 'C' shape and colours represent the Colorado mountains and landscape
- The gold represents the gold rush and natural resources
- Colorado adopted this flag in 1911

us-south-carolina.title: Flag of South Carolina
desc:
- A white palmetto tree and crescent moon on an indigo field
- The palmetto symbolises Colonel Moultrie's defence of Fort Sullivan (1776) built from palmetto logs
- **Construction:** an indigo blue field with a white crescent in the upper-hoist corner and a white palmetto tree centred
trivia:
- The palmetto represents South Carolina's coastal landscape and strength
- The crescent represents the crescent-shaped fortification (Fort Sumter)
- South Carolina adopted this flag in 1861

us-ohio.title: Flag of Ohio (Burgee)
desc:
- Ohio's flag is the only non-rectangular US state flag — a burgee (swallowtail) pennant. The red-white-blue design features a circle and 17 stars
- **Construction:** a swallowtail burgee (the only non-rectangular US state flag)
- A blue triangle based on the hoist extends into a red and white striped field (five stripes)
- A white circle with a red centre sits in the blue triangle; seventeen white stars surround it
trivia:
- The pennant design (not rectangular) is unique among US state flags
- The colours represent Ohio's history and natural resources
- Ohio adopted this flag in 1902

us-mississippi.title: Flag of Mississippi (In God We Trust)
desc:
- Adopted in 2021, replacing the Confederate-themed design. Features a magnolia blossom, "In God We Trust", and 21 stars
- **Construction:** three horizontal bands of dark blue, white, and red, with a white magnolia blossom on a dark blue field centred, surrounded by twenty-one white stars and the words 'In God We Trust'
- Adopted in 2021
trivia:
- Mississippi's flag previously featured the Confederate flag design; it was removed in 2020
- The current flag emphasizes the unity and future of the state
- Mississippi adopted its new flag design in 2021

us-georgia.title: Flag of Georgia (US state)
desc:
- Three horizontal stripes of red, white, and red with a blue canton containing the state coat of arms encircled by 13 white stars
- The current design was adopted on 8 May 2003 after years of controversy over previous flags
- The 13 stars represent Georgia as one of the original 13 colonies
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands (red-white-red)
- A blue canton in the upper-left with the state seal surrounded by 13 stars in a circle
- Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- The state seal shows the pillars of justice and wisdom
- The date 1776 represents Georgia's independence; 1799 represents the state constitution
- Georgia adopted this flag in 2003 after modifying it from a previous version
